title: CLO 2026.0 - Optimized Fitting Diagram
description: CLO 2026.0 version is now officially released — Make it, for real! The new version includes major updates to the fitting map section, such as strain maps based on fabric properties, toggling of fitting pressure map display effects, and saving fitting map attributes to project files. This video will explain all the details of the fitting map updates for you!
transcript:
In version Kolo 2026.0, we have made several major updates to the depth of field component, including the hardware image based on fabric attributes, the depth pressure image display effect toggle, and the storage of depth of field attributes within the project file, among others.

The following is a detailed introduction. First, the hardware image based on fabric attributes. Previously, some users may have noticed a discrepancy between the visual information shown in the hardware image and the actual results. We have now improved this by taking into account the physical characteristics of each fabric type, making it easier and more intuitive to check fabric stretch.

I will provide a detailed explanation through a visual document. Two types of fabrics are used in the visual document: the middle panel is covered with a single cloth, and the sides with a knitted fabric.

Now, let’s activate the hardware image.

In the vertical menu bar of the 3D window, you will see a depth chart icon. Here you can find the hardware image, hardware image, cloth image, and depth pressure image.

Click the hardware image icon to activate it. After activation, the hardware image window will appear at the top of the 2D window.

Before adjusting detailed properties of the hardware image, you need to enable the first option in the depth attribute to activate it.

However, in this version, the window appears immediately after activating the hardware image, making adjustments more convenient.

You can also explore new features in the hardware image.

Now, I will explain the difference between the two modes.

First, let's look at the general mode.

As before, the standard value is exactly the same for all fabrics.

The general mode is used to objectively check the physical deformation of the fabric itself, without considering the specific characteristics of the fabric.

The standard value of the fixed fabric can be freely adjusted and verified by dividing it into 8 segments.

When the user inputs the maximum value, the system automatically calculates the midpoint between the maximum and minimum values and divides it into 8 segments.

For example, if the maximum value is set to 120%, all fabrics that exceed this deformation point will be displayed in red.

Clicking any position on the garment allows you to check the specific hardware value at that point.

Therefore, the general mode operates based on the set ratio without considering the specific physical properties of the fabric.

At this point, I will manually change the maximum hardware value to 150% and simulate.

You will see the colors automatically adjust according to the new range.

Since the upper limit has increased, the red area significantly decreases.

Change it back to 120% and simulate again.

In this mode, when elastic fabric stretches beyond 120%, there is no issue with tightness when worn.

But because its stretch value exceeds the set standard, the system often displays it as red unconditionally.

As a result, it is impossible to judge differences based on the fabric’s maximum stretch strength.

In contrast, the fabric mode accounts for the fabric’s stretch strength.

The standard mode shows the maximum stretch strength of the fabric.

Based on the stretch strength calculated for the fabric, it represents the maximum stretch the fabric can sustain without further elongation when external force increases.

This way, you can check fabric consistency according to the maximum stretch strength of each fabric type, ensuring the fabric’s characteristics are accurately reflected.

The body’s condition is also clearer.

Now, let’s select fabric mode.

Similar to general mode, the visualization range divides the space between the 100% standard value and each fabric’s stretch limit into 8 segments.

The core difference from the general mode is the presence of a stretch limit area.

Here, the system automatically calculates and applies the limit range according to each fabric’s unique stretch characteristics.

This stretch limit represents a zero-sum value.

In other words, it can be understood as a turning point not considered too tight in actual wear.

For example, as shown,

the stretch limit value of the fabric is 138% at the front, 148% at the back, and 146% and 157% in the front.

The stretch limit of denim fabric is 103% at the front, 102% at the back, and 112% at the back.

Since the stretch values vary by fabric, simulation results differ from the general standard.

Let’s run the simulation and check the results.

Now, you can see the difference from the general mode.

The denim fabric used in the chest area has lower elasticity and has stretched to its limit.

Therefore, this area displays a tight state with a solid red bar.

Conversely, the highly elastic knitted fabric requires more stretch to reach its limit.

Thus, in the garment, it has not reached its limit, showing a solid blue bar, indicating a loose, non-tight state.

If you modify physical properties after applying fabric, the hardware image will not update these changes in real time.

Therefore, a refresh is required.

For example, if you replace the fabric with a different one or adjust its physical properties,

press the refresh button at the top right corner of the fabric panel to update the stretch values according to the modified fabric.

After launching the simulation, check the hard change values of the new fabric.

Because the stretch and limit values of this fabric are larger, most areas are displayed in blue.

You can also manually adjust the stretch limit.

Press this button to restore the original value.

To refresh stretch values for all fabrics, press the refresh button at the top.

Below is the display type modifier,

allowing you to set the hard change distribution style as you prefer.

It is roughly divided into gradient and area types.

If you want to clearly distinguish each area’s distribution, switch to the area type for inspection.

There are three display methods for each type: grid, surface, and peak.

Thus, you can freely choose how to check the hard change distribution type.

Next, let’s look at the hard change information function.

This function allows you to immediately check detailed values in the 3D window.

Click a specific point on the 3D garment.

A hard change information window will appear next to the mouse cursor.

I will explain it carefully.

First is the leading direction.

It shows the direction closest to the largest hard change at the selected point.

This indicator informs you about the fabric’s effect.

The limit value of the tail or shoes.

Which direction has the greatest stretch?

The actual stretch rate below is an absolute value.

It shows the extent of actual stretch in the fabric’s leading direction.

And the stretch rate.

Currently, the fabric’s largest stretch rate at the tail is observed.

The direction is the one with the greatest stretch.

We can confirm the stretch rate is approximately 111%.

Next is strength.

This value indicates the magnitude of the force applied at that point.

Expressed as a percentage, it means that under this force, the fabric’s maximum stretch rate at the tail is 130%.

This means an additional 23% force is applied.

The maximum stretch rate is 130%, while the fabric is stretched to 111%.

Click other positions to view corresponding hard change information.

Switch back to normal mode.

You can use any mode as needed.

But remember to remodel after switching modes.

Additionally, this function currently only applies to VR fabric.

Relevant VR fabric content was introduced in the new features of version 7.3.

The second half of the fabric generator function explanation is provided there.

Referring to that video may be helpful.

We will attach the video link in the comment section.

Use the improved fabric mode for hard change

to clearly reflect the simulation effects of each fabric characteristic.

Please try using this function in the new version to check the body effect.

In version 2026.0, a smooth display function has been added.

This function can more clearly show garments and models,

or, for example, the areas between seats

in states of close contact.

Let’s see how it works.

First, find the garment.

This is the depth attribute setting.

Look at the depth pressure option.

You can see that a smooth toggle has been added here.

In previous versions,

this function was not always enabled.

But in version 2026.0,

you can manually turn it on or off as needed.

As shown in the picture,

when the smooth function is enabled,

the point and surrounding points are displayed in gradient colors.

This means that even if some points’ values are outside the set range,

they may still be displayed in color.

This helps you more objectively determine the trend of fit between garments and models.

If smoothness is off,

points outside the defined range will not display color.

Only points that meet the criteria will be colored.

You can quickly identify the source of the problem.

It can also determine the spatial gap range between garments and models.

Now let’s go through the adjustment settings to learn more about this function.

First, turn off the smooth option.

At this time, the mid-range value is set to 0.1000p.

Open the simulation.

It can be observed that only pressure values reaching 0.1000p or above are colored.

Points in the mid-range do not show color because there is no contact or gap between garments and models.

Turn on smooth.

You will find that not only the target point but also surrounding points are displayed in gradient colors.

This simulates the expansion of physical pressure,

making the trend of affected areas clearer and more intuitive.

In version 2026.0,

users can flexibly control the smooth function’s on/off state according to their needs,

more objectively inspecting the gap between models and garments.

This establishes the situation and possibility of existence.

In version 2026.0,

hard drawing, hard change drawing, and deep drawing are all displayed directly on the 2D version.

Let’s use an example to understand this function.

First, go to the vertical menu bar on the left side of the 3D window.

Open the deep drawing option and select hard drawing.

After activation, the 3D garment will show strong and weak fabric pressure areas

with different color distributions.

At the same time, you will observe these pressure data are reflected similarly

on the 2D window version.

When switching to hard drawing or test drawing,

data in the 2D and 3D windows update simultaneously.

This helps you quickly and accurately locate large hard drawing or pressure-concentrated areas on the 2D version.

Using this method,

you can make more objective judgments about where adjustments are needed.

This update truly breaks the spatial and dimensional boundaries,

ensuring your 3D body analysis results

can be directly and accurately converted into 2D sample modification references.

In version 2026.0,

you can now save depth properties directly within the ZPRJ file.

This means your depth settings are tied to the garment,

ensuring team members working together

can check based on completely unified visual standards.

First, go to the 3D window.

In the vertical menu bar on the left,

open the depth option and select hard drawing.

Although this update applies to all depth settings,

we use hard drawing here as an example.

In the window settings,

adjust the range from 120% to 140%.

Open the simulation.

You will see colors in the 3D window immediately update

to reflect your default values.

Now just save the file as a project.

The default standards are also directly stored in the file.

Reopen the project file,

and the hard drawing will display the state you last saved,

so no need to adjust it again.

Our platform Closet also supports checking hard drawing.

These data can be perfectly synchronized with Closet.

Once you upload the file,

the test drawing settings on the platform automatically match your custom settings.

Through version 2026.0,

you can experience seamless synchronization of data within the project file,

ensuring visual consistency is maintained on Closet.

This is a smarter way to manage and share test drawing standards.

chunks.content: ## CLO 2026.0: Overview of Optimized Fitting Diagram Updates This document details the major updates in CLO version 2026.0 related to the depth of field component, focusing on fabric-based hardware image improvements, depth pressure image toggles, and saving depth attributes within project files. These enhancements improve fabric stretch visualization, fitting analysis, and team collaboration through unified data standards. --- ## Hardware Image Based on Fabric Attributes This section explains the improved hardware image feature that integrates fabric physical characteristics for more accurate and intuitive stretch visualization. ### Background and Activation Previously, the hardware image did not fully reflect fabric-specific physical properties, causing discrepancies between visual output and actual fabric behavior. CLO 2026.0 addresses this by incorporating fabric attributes into the hardware image rendering. - Access the hardware image via the **depth chart icon** in the 3D window's vertical menu. - The hardware image window appears atop the 2D window immediately upon activation. - Enable the first option in the depth attribute settings to activate detailed property adjustments. ### Fabric Example and Visualization A visual document compares two fabric types: - Middle panel: Single cloth fabric. - Side panels: Knitted fabric. Activating the hardware image clearly differentiates stretch behavior between these fabrics. --- ## General Mode vs. Fabric Mode in Hardware Image This section contrasts the two hardware image display modes—General and Fabric—and explains their calculation methods and visual outputs. ### General Mode - Uses a fixed standard value for all fabrics. - Focuses on objective physical deformation without fabric-specific considerations. - The stretch range is divided into 8 segments between minimum and maximum values. - Setting a maximum value (e.g., 120%) causes any fabric point exceeding this to display in red. - Example: Increasing max value to 150% reduces red areas, reflecting a looser fit. - Limitation: Elastic fabrics may show as overly tight (red) despite acceptable wear comfort, because stretch limits aren’t fabric-specific. ### Fabric Mode - Accounts for each fabric's unique maximum stretch strength (stretch limit). - Stretch limit represents the maximum sustainable stretch before irreversible elongation. - Visualization divides the range from 100% (standard) to each fabric’s stretch limit into 8 segments. - Example stretch limits: - Knitted fabric: 138%-157% across various points. - Denim fabric: 102%-112% range. - Simulations show denim areas reaching stretch limits (red tight zones) and knitted fabric areas remaining loose (blue). - Requires manual refresh after fabric property changes to update stretch visualization. - Allows manual reset of stretch limits to original values. ### Display Types and Styles - Two main distribution styles: **Gradient** and **Area**. - Three display methods for each style: **Grid**, **Surface**, and **Peak**. - Users can customize visualization to suit inspection needs. --- ## Hard Change Information Function This feature provides detailed fabric stretch data for specific garment points in the 3D window. ### Key Metrics Displayed - **Leading Direction**: Direction of the largest stretch at the selected point. - **Actual Stretch Rate**: Absolute stretch percentage in the leading direction.

chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - Optimized Fitting Diagram
chunks.content: ### Display Types and Styles - Two main distribution styles: **Gradient** and **Area**. - Three display methods for each style: **Grid**, **Surface**, and **Peak**. - Users can customize visualization to suit inspection needs. --- ## Hard Change Information Function This feature provides detailed fabric stretch data for specific garment points in the 3D window. ### Key Metrics Displayed - **Leading Direction**: Direction of the largest stretch at the selected point. - **Actual Stretch Rate**: Absolute stretch percentage in the leading direction. - **Stretch Rate**: Fabric’s largest stretch rate, indicating current elongation. - **Strength**: Force magnitude at the point, expressed as a percentage of maximum stretch capacity (e.g., 130% max stretch with 111% current stretch indicates 23% additional force). ### Usage Notes - Click any garment point in 3D to view detailed hard change info. - Switch between modes (general/fabric) as needed; remodeling is required after switching. - This function currently supports only VR fabric types (introduced in version 7.3). --- ## Smooth Display Function for Depth Pressure This section describes the new smooth display toggle that enhances visualization of garment-model contact and pressure distribution. ### Functionality - Located in the **depth pressure** option within depth attribute settings. - When **enabled**, point values and surrounding points show gradient colors. - Helps visualize trends and spatial gaps between garments and models more intuitively. - When **disabled**, only points meeting threshold criteria display color, aiding quick problem identification. ### Example Usage - With smooth off and mid-range set to 0.1000p, only points with pressure ≥0.1000p are colored. - Turning smooth on adds gradient coloring to adjacent points, simulating pressure spread. ### Benefits - Users can flexibly toggle smoothness for objective inspection of fit and contact areas. - Enhances understanding of close contact zones, especially in tight-fitting sections. --- ## Integration of 2D and 3D Hard Drawing Visualizations This section covers simultaneous display and synchronization of hard drawing (pressure visualization) across 2D and 3D views. ### Features - Accessible via the vertical menu bar in the 3D window under **deep drawing**. - Selecting **hard drawing** shows strong/weak fabric pressure areas with color coding on both 3D garment and 2D pattern windows. - Data updates simultaneously in both windows when switching display types. - Enables quick, accurate localization of pressure-concentrated areas on 2D patterns. - Bridges spatial and dimensional gaps between 3D body analysis and 2D sample adjustments. --- ## Saving Depth Properties Within Project Files (.ZPRJ) This crucial update allows storing all depth of field settings directly in the project file for seamless collaboration and consistency. ### Workflow - Adjust depth settings (e.g., hard drawing range from 120% to 140%) in the 3D window. - Start simulation to apply settings visually. - Save the project file (.ZPRJ); all depth attributes and visual standards are saved. - Reopening the project restores saved settings automatically, eliminating the need for repeated adjustments. ### Collaboration and Platform Integration - CLO’s platform **Closet** supports synchronized checking of hard drawing.

chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - Optimized Fitting Diagram
chunks.content: --- ## Saving Depth Properties Within Project Files (.ZPRJ) This crucial update allows storing all depth of field settings directly in the project file for seamless collaboration and consistency. ### Workflow - Adjust depth settings (e.g., hard drawing range from 120% to 140%) in the 3D window. - Start simulation to apply settings visually. - Save the project file (.ZPRJ); all depth attributes and visual standards are saved. - Reopening the project restores saved settings automatically, eliminating the need for repeated adjustments. ### Collaboration and Platform Integration - CLO’s platform **Closet** supports synchronized checking of hard drawing. - Uploaded project files retain custom test drawing settings on Closet. - Ensures unified visual standards across team members and platforms. - Enhances management and sharing of test drawing standards with smart synchronization. --- # Summary CLO 2026.0 introduces significant improvements to fabric stretch visualization and fitting analysis through: - Hardware images reflecting fabric-specific physical properties. - Two distinct visualization modes (General and Fabric) with adjustable stretch limits. - Detailed hard change information for precise fabric force and stretch data. - A smooth display toggle for better depth pressure interpretation. - Synchronized 2D and 3D hard drawing displays for accurate pressure localization. - Saving depth attribute settings within project files for consistent, collaborative workflows. Users are encouraged to utilize these features for more objective, fabric-aware fitting simulations and enhanced project standardization.
